dialogue:
Speaker1: Alright, let me talk about summer foods.
Speaker1: I usually eat red bean shaved ice in the summer. Red bean shaved ice is really tasty, I think. I often go to Sulbing, or just eat regular red bean shaved ice a lot, but my favorite at Sulbing is the chocolate shaved ice. Anything chocolate-related is just great.
Speaker1: I mean, I like chocolate strawberry bingsu and stuff like chocolate Oreo too. I'm kinda into chocolate a lot.
Speaker1: So, do you not eat much patbingsu in the summer?
Speaker2: I’m more of a fruit person than a bingsu fan, I guess.
Speaker2: I always wanna eat peaches and watermelon when spring turns to summer, but they get super pricey then.
Speaker2: The reason I always look forward to summer is enjoying watermelon while feeling the breeze from the fan and air conditioner, watching TV—those moments are the best, and I think those memories are the most precious in summer.
Speaker2: Do you know the term "eoljuga"?
Speaker1: Is it like "freezing to death"? Like, "I’ll eat ice cream even if I’m freezing"?
Speaker2: Oh, not quite. It means you drink iced coffee or iced drinks no matter how cold it is.
Speaker2: I weirdly get really cold in winter, but I always end up drinking iced drinks. It just feels the best to have ice cream or a cold drink on a chilly day. It’s such a refreshing vibe.
Speaker1: I also feel really good eating ice cream when it's cold.
Speaker1: Honestly, it’s tasty in summer, but eating one or two ice creams at home when it’s cold in winter is just the best.
Speaker1: So, I had ice cream yesterday, the Bianco kind. But I’m not really into the apple sorbet underneath, so I just enjoyed the vanilla on top.
Speaker1: I feel like ice cream's good anytime, like now when it's spring heading into summer, or in the fall, or even winter. It's always tasty.

Speaker1: So, what comes to mind for you when you think of winter?
Speaker2: For me, Christmas is always the highlight of winter. It’s super cold, but the vibe is so warm, and everyone looks happy, smiling, and enjoying cake and good food together. I just love that cozy atmosphere, so I find myself looking forward to Christmas even in the summer.
Speaker2: Do you like Christmas?
Speaker1: I really love Christmas. The carols and that special vibe just feel so good, and I definitely get this exciting feeling when I think about Christmas.
Speaker1: But when I think about it, I don’t really do anything special for Christmas. I mean, it’s more like I just hang out at home or meet up with friends and do the same stuff we usually do, like going to Seomyeon or Nampo-dong, or maybe working part-time. But I guess it’s still nice, always the same.
Speaker1: It's nice that even though I spend it the same way every year, Christmas still feels special. I really like Christmas.
Speaker1: So, what do you think about Chuseok in the fall?
Speaker2: I didn't really like Chuseok when I was a kid. It was always about hanging out with relatives for a couple of days, but then there was always that goodbye afterward, you know? So I didn't want to go when Chuseok came around, and I was kinda scared of that goodbye, so I tried to avoid it.
Speaker2: Now I actually look forward to Chuseok since I rarely get to see my relatives, and it’s nice to see my grandma again.
Speaker2: Do you have any memories or thoughts about Chuseok?
Speaker1: Yeah, I really like Chuseok too. There’s so much good food, and it feels great to see relatives and my mom's side of the family after a while.
Speaker1: It's kinda fun seeing how everyone changes when we meet up, like some folks looking super happy after passing a test or others who seem to have lost some weight. Those chats are always a good time.
Speaker1: And when I think of Chuseok, the most memorable stuff is definitely from when I was a kid.
Speaker1: I think my best memories of Chuseok are playing Nintendo with my cousins since I usually played alone at home, but when we got together, we’d do multiplayer, eat good food, and stay up all night.
Speaker1: So, what do you think about Lunar New Year in winter?
Speaker2: I haven't really seen my relatives on New Year's for the past couple of years, 'cause I was either abroad or just couldn't make it.
Speaker2: So now, I only have a few bittersweet memories of Lunar New Year.
Speaker2: So, do you like Lunar New Year?
Speaker1: I kinda like Lunar New Year, same vibe as Chuseok.
Speaker1: Lunar New Year feels fresh, like really fresh, you know?
Speaker1: I guess since New Year's only comes once a year, it feels even more special.
Speaker1: Yeah, you get to eat a lot of good food and see people you haven’t in a while, so it’s definitely a memorable time. New Year’s is great.

Speaker1: What’s the last gift you gave someone?
Speaker2: I've been baking a ton of cookies to give as gifts lately. I guess since I graduated high school in baking and pastry, it just feels the most rewarding to make bread or something for someone, and it makes me feel really good too.
Speaker2: Have you given or received any gifts recently?
Speaker1: I recently gave a gift to my parents, that's the most recent one.
Speaker1: I just started my part-time job not long ago, so this is the first time I’m using my own money, not just allowance, even if it’s not a huge amount.
Speaker1: I wanted to get my parents something with that money.
Speaker1: So I really thought about what to give them. I’ve spent a lot of time with my mom and dad, but nothing came to mind for a gift. I figured I’d just give them some cash, but putting it in an envelope or doing a bank transfer felt too much like just giving them allowance. I wanted it to feel more like a gift, so I got a box with those fake flowers—what do you even call them?
Speaker1: Yeah. I got a box with fake flowers and rolled up money all pretty, and I gave that to my parents separately.
Speaker1: Yeah, they really liked it, and it’s the most memorable gift I’ve given recently.
Speaker1: So, what’s the most memorable gift you’ve given?
Speaker2: I think giving perfume is my most memorable gift. It's because I always remember people by their scent or can tell them apart by it.
Speaker2: So, when I think of someone, I’m like, “Oh, that person has that smell,” or “This person has this smell,” and I always remember that, so when I’m gifting friends, perfume is usually my go-to.
Speaker2: Fragrances or scented products are always my top choice.
Speaker2: So, it’s not the most recent, but uh, tomorrow’s my friend’s birthday, so I’m meeting up today, and I’m gonna get them a perfume as a gift.

Speaker1: Do you like perfume as a gift?
Speaker2: I’ve gotten perfume as a gift before. It was last year, and I really dislike certain scents but love good ones, so I don’t think I’ve ever gotten a perfume I really liked.
Speaker2: I’m not a fan of strong scents, so if it’s something that others might not find overpowering but I think is too intense, it just doesn’t sit right with me.
Speaker2: I mean, I felt good about getting a gift, but I don’t really remember liking the perfume itself.
Speaker2: Yeah, I don’t really use perfume; I pay more attention to body mist or body wash stuff.
Speaker2: So, do you have a most memorable perfume gift?
Speaker1: The most memorable gift for me was, uh, I actually remember the body mist more than perfume. Last year for my birthday, a friend got me this gift box from a brand called Lush. It had bath bombs, body wash, and a little body mist in it. The scent was really nice, and since it’s my favorite brand, I think that’s why it’s the best gift I remember.
Speaker1: Thinking about it, giving perfume as a gift really means you gotta know the person's taste super well and how much they actually like it. It's kinda tricky, but when you give it and they feel all proud, that's the best feeling.
Speaker1: I graduated from baking and pastry, so I love making handmade food gifts. Do you like giving gifts like that too?
Speaker2: When I was in elementary school, I wanted to give chocolate to a boy I liked for Valentine's Day, so I bought all the ingredients to make it myself. But since I'm not really good with my hands, I ended up failing and just gave him store-bought chocolate.
Speaker2: I've tried to make stuff a bunch of times since then, but I always fail.
Speaker2: Yeah, since elementary school, I haven't really thought about making something special to give.
Speaker2: What’s the most memorable handmade gift you’ve made?
Speaker1: I remember making homemade ginger tea as a gift. A friend of mine was really struggling with a bad cold, so I found online that ginger tea is good for that, and I made it for them along with a note to help them get better.
Speaker1: Uh, making something like that isn’t too hard. Would you be interested in trying it out?
Speaker2: Yeah, hearing you talk makes me wanna do something nice for the adults around me. They’d probably be really touched.
Speaker2: If I were an adult and someone made me something like homemade syrup, or really anything, I’d feel super grateful.
Speaker2: It's not just a gift; something made for you really sticks in your memory. Like, my friend once made me a flower pot cake back when it was a trend, about ten years ago. They crushed up Oreos and put it all together, and it really stands out to me. They even added little gummy worms on top, which was such a nice touch. It felt great! Honestly, making something for someone just makes both the giver and receiver feel good.

Speaker1: So, do you have any memorable events or anything like that you’ve experienced?
Speaker2: I feel like I mostly just remember planning events with friends for special occasions instead of actually receiving them.
Speaker2: So, when I recently went to Jeju and met up with a friend after a long time, we celebrated by getting balloons and stuff for New Year’s, like 2020 balloons and “Happy New Year” ones, and we took a ton of pictures together. I was there for about 4 nights and 5 days, but honestly, that little time felt like the most precious time to me.
Speaker2: We talked a lot while blowing up the balloons and laughed a ton taking pictures.
Speaker2: Then after that, eating something delicious with my friend made it an even better memory, and it stuck with me nicely.
Speaker2: Do you have a favorite event you've received?
Speaker1: Oh, the most memorable event I’ve been a part of was the one I got for my birthday in elementary school.
Speaker1: We had this thing where my close friends would do little events for each other's birthdays.
Speaker1: So my friends threw me an event at school when no one was around on the weekend, kinda like Running Man, and it was a really unique experience.
Speaker1: That was the most memorable, unique, and kinda weird event I’ve had.
Speaker1: I think the gifts I got when I was really young are super precious. What’s the most memorable gift you got as a kid?
Speaker2: Honestly, when I think back to my childhood, it’s less about getting gifts and more about hanging out with friends after school, playing on the playground. I kinda struggle to remember any specific gifts.
Speaker2: I really wanna do something like that with my friends someday after watching that show.
Speaker2: Do you wanna do any cool events like that on your birthday?
Speaker1: Well, I don't really have anything specific, but if I had to say, I kinda wish something unique and different would happen on my birthday. Yeah, I've thought about it since I was a kid. I like unexpected things, even if they're not necessarily good.
Speaker1: I kinda miss that, and I’d love to do something like that too.
Speaker1: So, do you have any plans to give someone a gift soon?
Speaker2: So, there's this girl I know whose birthday is around mid-June, and I've been thinking about making one of those lettered lunchbox cakes that are super popular on Instagram as a gift.

Speaker1: I can't really remember my childhood dreams, though.
Speaker1: Do you remember your dreams from when you were a kid, name?
Speaker2: When I was little, my dream changed a lot. First, in kindergarten, I wanted to be a cop.
Speaker2: Yeah, back then all the kids thought being a cop was cool, but honestly, I didn’t think it was that great. I wasn’t really into it, but since everyone wanted to be a cop or president or congressman, I guess that’s why I wanted to be a cop in kindergarten.
Speaker2: I wanted to be a chef in elementary school.
Speaker2: So in elementary school, I wanted to be a chef because my cousin was this super talented chef who competed in international contests and all that. He was like the youngest national representative or something, and I guess I wanted to be a chef too since everyone was so impressed by him.
Speaker2: In middle school, I wanted to be a pro gamer since I was really into games.
Speaker2: I guess I didn’t really have a dream back then. Just kinda went with the flow like everyone else, and when it came time to prep for the college entrance exam in senior year, it felt overwhelming trying to find a realistic dream.
Speaker2: So, did your dreams change a lot since you were a kid?
Speaker1: You said your dream changed every day when you were little.
Speaker1: So whenever they asked us to write down our future dreams at school, my parents always wrote it for me. My mom would just put down "teacher," and I thought, "Oh, I guess I could be that," but as I grew up and started studying more, I realized, "Yeah, I can't be a teacher."
Speaker1: So I guess I just kinda ended up thinking realistically about getting a job at a company.
Speaker1: So, yeah, there’s a big difference between dreams you can actually achieve and the ones you can’t.
Speaker1: So, do you have a dream that feels possible right now and one that seems kinda impossible but you really want to achieve?
Speaker2: Yeah, I’ve got realistic dreams and some unrealistic ones. The unrealistic ones are just like winning the lottery and living easy as a rich bum, passing down money to my kids and donating in style, maybe even making it into the news. But my realistic dreams aren’t that realistic either; the process to get to those goals is super tough.
Speaker2: I kinda wanna be successful and a good person, making a lot of money, but I also have this ambition for recognition. So, I want to get to a high position and give talks, sharing how I grew and showing others they can do it too. That's my realistic dream.
Speaker2: So, I’m still figuring things out, and honestly, I’m looking into other paths too.
Speaker2: Can you share what dreams you might have for when you're older?
Speaker1: Well, I haven't really thought about what I'll be doing in the future since I haven't achieved any of my dreams yet. I’ve imagined a bit about what I might be like in a few decades, but I don’t think I’ve ever seriously considered it. Still, if there’s something I hope for...
Speaker1: I kinda wanna try farming, you know? Just a simple life, growing my own food with someone special.
Speaker1: So, I guess to really do that farming thing, you need a decent amount of money these days, right? You gotta have a house and land, so to make that dream happen in old age, I need to earn some cash now, but I'm not really good at making money, so it feels like a pretty unrealistic dream.
Speaker1: So, do you have any dreams for your golden years, name?
Speaker2: I wanna farm in the countryside when I’m older, build a nice house, live comfortably with family, and just enjoy a peaceful, healthy life without any drama.
Speaker2: I wanna do some volunteering in my old age and run a café. Just chillin' in the countryside during the week and volunteering on weekends, you know? Sounds nice, right?
Speaker2: I wanna have a nice, peaceful old age, running a little café where not too many people come, and just living that dream.

Speaker1: Do you remember any family dreams or anything?
Speaker1: So, I remember my parents' dreams, like my siblings' and stuff.
Speaker1: My mom wanted to be a broadcaster since I was little.
Speaker1: She really wanted to be an announcer, so she’d bring newspapers and read them to us, saying that’s how you practice pronunciation.
Speaker1: And I grew up seeing my mom's dream of wanting to be a newscaster, but realistically, she couldn't achieve it.
Speaker1: I hoped my sister would go that route, but she's not into it; she's all about cartoons and music.
Speaker1: So, I've been into music since I was a kid, always singing Japanese songs at home and recording them.
Speaker1: So my sister's dream is to be a composer now, and she's working hard on her songs, but she hasn't really made it big yet, so I think she's feeling a lot of pressure from our parents and it's kinda tough for her.
Speaker1: So, I've thought about pursuing something like that too, since my family had those dreams.
Speaker1: Any family dreams you remember?
Speaker2: Oh, earlier you mentioned name, right? Well, I’ve thought about family dreams too, and first...
Speaker2: My mom wanted to be a writer when she was younger, especially a children's book author, since she was pretty sensitive and had some talent. But because of tough family circumstances, she gave up on that dream and now she's just an office worker.
Speaker2: But my dad is the type who actually achieved his dream. He originally wanted to be a navigator, so he went to maritime university and really sailed ships. But since it takes a long time to operate a ship and it’s such a lonely job, he has a different dream and job now, but I think he definitely fulfilled his dream.
Speaker2: Oh, and earlier you mentioned wanting to run a café—are you thinking about a franchise or a personal one?
Speaker1: I’d rather run a personal café than a franchise. With a franchise, you’ve got to stick to their brand and recipes, which can be limiting. I want to set up my café the way I like, create my own menu, and attract customers based on my style. I think skill matters more than with a franchise. As long as I can make a living, I’m cool with running a personal café more as a hobby, not stressing about making a ton of money. So yeah, that’s why I want to go for a personal café.
Speaker1: By the way, do you remember any of your friends' dreams?
Speaker2: So, one of my friends always wanted to help and care for others since we were kids. At first, they wanted to be a doctor, but then it gradually changed to wanting to be a nurse, and finally, right before senior year, they decided to become a physical therapist. Now, they're working as a physical therapist.
Speaker2: It's nice to see my friend achieve their dream, so I'm feeling good about it. Do you have any memories of your friends' dreams?
Speaker1: I had a junior in the army who dreamed of being a vet. He was really into animals, always looking up books and studying about them even on weekends.
Speaker1: So, my friend’s working at a factory now, but originally wanted to start a business, so he joined to save up some cash, but it’s not going well, and now he’s thinking of switching it up.

Speaker1: It's been a little over six months since we broke up.
Speaker1: Ugh, it’s been forever since I dated a guy, and I’m seriously craving one.
Speaker1: I really wanna date and just walk around with my arm linked with someone like everyone else, but I’m so scared of meeting new guys after getting hurt by my exes. Ugh, I’m seriously stressing about what kind of guy I should even go for.
Speaker1: What kind of guy do you think would be more my style?
Speaker2: I mean, with all the bad stuff happening lately, like dating violence and whatnot in the news, I'm kinda interested in dating, but it’s also scary.
Speaker2: I guess I’m thinking maybe I should meet some people first, see their personality, and if I like them, then go for it.
Speaker2: I mean, it’s nice if he’s good-looking, right? Like, if my boyfriend is always handsome, that’s a plus.
Speaker2: But if I get caught up in looks and end up with a bad personality, I’m the one who suffers.
Speaker2: So, like, people are doing those speed dating things lately, right?
Speaker2: I think it’s better to get to know someone over time and then date, rather than just meeting up on the spot.
Speaker2: So, like, don’t you have any close guy friends around these days? Someone worth keeping an eye on?
Speaker1: Honestly, I’m kinda like you—what do they call it, “natural dating”? I tend to go for that too. I’d rather get to know someone a bit first and see if they’re a good person before I start developing feelings.
Speaker1: But there's this older guy I'm kinda into lately. You know, the church guy.
Speaker1: That whole thing about not checking compatibility? The age gap of four years is pretty awesome.
Speaker1: But when I check out guys, I don’t really look at their faces.
Speaker1: Most people think it's a lie when you say you don't care about looks, but my exes can back me up on this.
Speaker1: My exes all had pretty average looks, but I seriously don’t care about that at all.
Speaker1: Ugh, I seriously fall in love way too easily. Like, I'm such a sucker for it.
Speaker1: I've liked this guy for a while now.
Speaker1: It's been over six months since we broke up, right? Not long after that, I started to kinda like him.
Speaker1: Ugh, that guy's really great, but he's a total dealbreaker—he's a virgin. I've been burned by too many virgins before, so I promised myself I wouldn't date another one, but here we are. What do I do? I'm seriously stressing over this.
Speaker1: You know those times when you really like someone, but they don’t match your ideal type? And your ideal type is shaped by your experiences? I just don’t know what to do in those situations.
Speaker1: Think about it, what would you do? You really like this guy, but he doesn't match your ideal type. What would you do?
Speaker2: I’d probably just wait and see, you know?
Speaker2: If I see that his strengths totally outweigh his weaknesses, then I’d probably date him, but being a virgin is such a dealbreaker. It might just overshadow everything else, so I’d definitely think about it a bit more.
Speaker2: 'Cause I'm a person too, you know? I've dated before. Everyone's got their own story—some are total newbies, some have dated a bit. But I ended up dating someone who was a total newbie last time.
Speaker2: I get why you're struggling with this, for real.
Speaker2: But I'm really curious about something—since you mentioned older guys, your brother, right?
Speaker2: So, do you prefer older guys? Have all your past partners been older?
Speaker1: Nah, unfortunately, my type's never matched up.
Speaker1: Ugh, I’m so sad right now. I feel like I’m gonna cry. My vision’s getting all blurry.
Speaker1: Aw, it really sucks that I've never met an older guy.
Speaker1: I've definitely had my share of flings, but when it comes to actual relationships, they're all younger or the same age.
Speaker1: I'm just looking for someone a bit more mature and responsible, you know? Someone who can take care of me and really support me, that's my type.
Speaker1: I mean, it’s not a hard rule, but generally, older guys fit that bill a bit better, right?
Speaker1: For real, I just wanna meet someone older, but everyone I end up with is younger or my age. I'm the one doing all the caring. Your ex was a total noob too, right? My last ex was a noob as well. What’s the point of me teaching them if they’re just gonna use it on someone else? Seriously.
Speaker1: I seriously just wanna meet an older guy so bad. And the guy I like is older too, but he’s not interested in me at all.
Speaker1: He has no idea I like him, and neither does anyone else at church.
Speaker1: No one knows, seriously, not a single person.
Speaker1: I’m so low-key about who I like, but maybe I should drop a hint or something.
Speaker1: Kinda bummed he has no clue I like him, you know?
Speaker1: It kinda stings when he treats me just like any other little sister, you know?
Speaker1: Ugh, if I show any signs, I feel like he’ll get uncomfortable and pull away, and then I’d lose that connection with him. That really worries me.
Speaker1: Ugh, should I confess or not? Should I show I like him or not? I’m always stressing about it, but I still haven’t said anything. Should I or shouldn’t I? For real.
Speaker1: If you had a guy you liked who’s really close with you, would you confess? 'Cause if you do, it feels like it might mess up your relationship, but if you don’t, it’s like your heart’s just aching. What would you do?
Speaker2: I’d probably drop hints. You gotta, like, let it out. If you just keep it all bottled up and then suddenly decide to confess, that person might be totally caught off guard, you know?
Speaker2: So, to prepare for that, you should drop a hint like, "I kinda love you," right? And...
Speaker2: If you approach them with love, they might pull away a bit, but if you get your feelings sorted and come at them as a friend, who knows? You might end up liking them even more or it could turn into something meaningful.
Speaker2: Actually, I used to date this guy who was a total loner, and we're getting along great. I thought it might be tough for us to be in a relationship for some reason, so I suggested we go back to being friends, and he was cool with it. We're still doing really well. I even hung out at his place when I went to Seoul recently.
Speaker2: It kinda depends on the person; if someone feels pressured about love, it can keep feeling that way.
Speaker2: But you don’t really know that part, right? I think it’d be good to learn more about it.
Speaker2: That's just part of their personality, so it's up to you whether you can accept that or not.
Speaker2: So, to wrap it up, I think you should make a move and show some interest.
Speaker2: So, do you have a solid reason to think that if that person really loves you, they’d pull away?
Speaker2: I feel like if I show I'm really into them, it'll push them away, so I thought there must be a reason for that, right?
Speaker1: He's super popular, like, for real.
Speaker1: A close friend of mine has shown that she likes him, and you know how church people are—they always try to set up couples, but he finds it really overwhelming.
Speaker1: That guy's really feeling the pressure, and since he's super close with that girl, they’re the same age, he’s getting all stiff and avoiding her.
Speaker1: Ugh, seeing that just makes me even more hesitant. What if I actually show I like him and then he moves away? He's just about to graduate and is probably thinking about whether to stay here or go back home.
Speaker1: What if I do this and he leaves the area? I’d be so bummed I’d cry.
Speaker1: Ugh, what do I do? I'm kinda scared, honestly. I mean, liking him is my choice, but I'm worried he might feel really pressured if I show it.
Speaker1: But you said earlier, right? I just don’t get how you can still be close with your ex. I think once you break up, it’s natural to be worse than strangers. How can you be friends with an ex?
Speaker1: I really try to understand, but I just can’t.
Speaker1: 'Cause I've never had a good breakup with an ex. It's always one person getting tired, one losing interest, or both fighting.
Speaker1: So usually, one person’s feelings are definitely still there, right?
Speaker1: If you start with feelings for someone, but as you date, you see more flaws than good stuff, right? If those flaws keep piling up, you get tired of them and your love fades, so you leave. At that point, all the good stuff is gone, so how can you see the good in them again?
Speaker1: I don’t get that. How can you do that?
Speaker2: So, like you said earlier, it's a slow burn. We started as friends and then dated, so it was easier to go back to being friends, you know?
Speaker2: At first, it was kinda awkward, and we didn’t talk much, just me occasionally messaging, but then I got my feelings sorted out and started chatting comfortably, and they did the same.
Speaker2: Plus, I asked for understanding. I told them I have these feelings and it’d be tough to date, so I wanted to break up to avoid things getting worse, and they respected that. I think that’s why it worked out better for us.

Speaker1: What kind of student were you back in school?
Speaker2: I was kinda just a quiet student, nothing special really.
Speaker2: I mean, I wasn't super shy or anything, but I just got along fine with everyone and stayed out of trouble, you know?
Speaker2: Looking back, I kinda wish I had made more memories and been a bit more active in school.
Speaker2: So, I guess my friends and I are still getting along pretty well.
Speaker2: I guess I had a pretty chill school life, even keeping in touch with some teachers now and then.
Speaker2: What kind of student were you?
Speaker1: I was a really quiet student too. Kinda funny to say, but I was like, barely noticeable in class.
Speaker1: Not like I studied hard or anything, though.
Speaker1: Kinda feel like I was a bit slacking, to be honest.
Speaker1: I mean, I made some good friends, but I haven't really kept in touch with them, so I kinda regret that part of my friendships.
Speaker1: I mostly liked going to the library when I was in school.
Speaker1: What did you like most about school outside of the classroom?
Speaker2: I’m the opposite of you.
Speaker2: I don’t think I liked the library much. I actually preferred sitting on a bench outside with the kids, chatting and playing around in the breeze.
Speaker2: I think it was a school where even though we were different schools, we could see boys and girls playing together on the same playground. That was kinda fun, and I guess the teachers were more careful about it too.
Speaker2: I think I relieved a lot of stress hanging out with friends outside or at the snack bar, eating the food there and just chatting, rather than spending time in the classroom or library.
Speaker2: And our school had a computer lab too, so I have fun memories of playing games and practicing on the computers there.
Speaker2: What was your favorite subject, Speaker1?
Speaker1: I think my favorite subject was Korean since I was more into the humanities.
Speaker1: I wasn't really good at math or science, and I didn't find them interesting, so my grades were always pretty bad.
Speaker1: I guess I ended up working harder at what I liked since I always did well in Korean.
Speaker1: But on the flip side, I didn’t do well in English, so even now in college, those classes stress me out a lot.
